svg.title: BERR: code-based architecture and spatial restoration mechanisms
svg.desc: Architecture reviewed against Beyond Glare commit ad76b408a8b1130f70d9253d14a765e67f5e380d. The batch dimension is omitted. A single encoder processes four aligned RGB-plus-geometry ROIs, at 128x128x32, 64x64x64 and 32x32x128. Per-scale softmax fusion uses resized shallow-feature degradation logits. Anchor and fused features are concatenated at all three decoder scales; a 6-channel residual head yields visible/prior RGB ROIs after tanh, addition to the anchor ROI, and clipping. Sigmoid masks define both the all-degraded product and the anchor degradation mask. Local compositing and masked feathered paste produce the final anchor-coordinate frame. Residual-flow refinement is disabled in the checked configuration. Photographic inputs, saved prior/restored ROIs, ground-truth reference, and masks a/p come from the existing validation diagnostic for sample 5987_gpt_v00, checkpoint epoch 57, step 20862. That validation set uses synthetic glare on photographic faces. Only frame 0 is shown; rear input sheets represent the four-frame dimension. Feature sheets, spatial weight maps, and RGB intermediate symbols are schematics. The visible head V and first blend S were not exported and are shown as tensor symbols. At the user’s request, the two final full-face thumbnails show the Ground Truth tile as a target reference for Y, not the model’s Final Output. This is an architecture schematic of the intended ideal restoration; the target photos are not measured model outputs. Labels Y and Restored Y denote the output of the architecture; source provenance is recorded here rather than in visible diagram text. No new inference was run. Anchor and aligned-ROI display thumbnails are direct uniformly scaled crops of the full input photograph, without using the distorted diagnostic ROI tile. The display rectangle x=30,y=98,w=191,h=59 comes from metadata/000005_hq5987_b0.json; matching the exported anchor ROI confirms the corresponding input crop. Saved normalized prior/restored predictions are reprojected into that same image-space display rectangle, not treated as unresized originals. The code still crops then resizes each ROI to 128x128; the diagram labels this resize explicitly. Masks remain in normalized ROI coordinates.
